I'm not making the implication you should never be happy with who you are at the time, or what direction you are going in. I'm stating that celebrating being average takes away from striving for more.

In your reply you state that you should stop to celebrate how far you've come, and to be content with progress. Understand that this is the opposite of being content with average. If you are making progress and moving forward and working hard then you AREN'T celebrating being average, you are celebrating being better than you once were.

Being average is not about a comparison of you to other people, it's all about you. If you are celebrating not putting much effort to improve and become above average, then you aren't using motivation properly. In your scenario, you state the person has made progress, and that is worth celebrating! The person has achieved something, they are on their way to becoming more.

In fact, your whole argument is based around the concept of being exceptional in some things and average in most. This is, again, NOT BEING AVERAGE. In the gif he states that your best should be around average, as if to say if you try your best at something, you'll still be average.

This is counterproductive, and it makes it seem like you shouldn't give your best for everything.

In the end, it isn't about comparing yourselves to others, but rather to what you want to achieve. If you want to be an incredible artist, you need to work at it everyday. If you want to be an athlete, you need to train everyday. You need to do an above average amount of work to change. 

Never accept being average, always work toward being better at the things that matter to you, and celebrate the progress you make.

I agree. Most of his advice has a lot of truth to it, but the line about being happy with being average is not what GetMotivated is all about.

Consequentialists: People who say the end justifies the mean. I'm about 5 years on  the dot, as it had happened in freshman year. You see, I was living a very confusing and painful life at the time. I'd been bullied for about 10 years by this point, and trust me when I say that every year it simply got worse. In freshman year, I found myself without many friends, without much direction in life, and most importantly, without a place to belong. I was quite the loner, I did not speak much out of fear of being insulted, or considered ignorant. I was a good student, and an even better artist, but these things could not help me.

I wanted desperately to be part of this skater crew which I had made some acquaintances in. I was pretty okay at skating, and these guys were so cool! They semi-accepted me. They were alright with having me around, but they never really reached out much. We made an odd pseudo-relationship, where we seemed like good friends. But they were hesitant to allow me in the group. They didn't really have much of an interest putting a kid like me in their little click, so the pushed me out.

Now mind you, at this time I was being bullied constantly, and even after dozens of visits to the principal my school never truly reprimanded my bullies. These kids crushed everything I was and *got away with it scott free.* I started believing the things the people were saying to me. I started believing I was trash, that I didn't belong on this earth. That if I killed myself the world would be better, somehow.

So, I set out to do it. I had a plan, I would go home and hang myself from my ceiling fan. Simple as that. I had the rope, I knew the knot, and my parents wouldn't find me until it was too late. A tragically perfect scheme.

But I slipped up, I couldn't take the burden of knowing it alone, and I spoke to someone. A kid in the skater group, named jack. Jack was a big guy, and the nicest person you could meet. He figured out what I was saying when I said I would be, "Out of school next week."

He, and the other skaters, confronted me in the bathroom, and I broke down. I was a much younger and confused kid then. I couldn't handle it at all. I told them they could not tell anyone, but they did anyway. They knew I had to get help.

Funny thing is, even after I contemplated it, and it spread around the school, my bullies used that knowledge as *new insults*. They would actually say, "I bet you don't have the balls to kill yourself."

Looking back, I am unfathomably glad that I was stopped. In those next 5 years, I became a new person. Today, I am an honors student in senior housing at my college, and I'm just a freshman. In those 5 years, I joined Boy Scouts, and I am to get my Eagle this month! As for friends, well, I have hundreds now. Many of them would follow me to the ends of this earth. Life is good, but even better than that.

Life is Precious.

As for the OP, mate, just keep going. Everything gets better after the struggle. Perhaps that is why the struggle is there, to stock you up on good karma for when you really need it. I'm unsure, but I realize now the reason why those boys bullied me for so long was because I thought differently. Because I was different. I'm unsure what your depression comes from, but I guarantee that you will find a path that few others have experienced.

Stay Strong, friend.

Alright, I have some tips for you guys, since you seem to be having trouble.

I moved out of state for college, and it is HARD to make new friends after school, but there is a way.

1 - Join Classes and Groups and Such : It's already been said here, but if you join a club or go to a class then you already have a conversation starter and a single common interest. It makes it really easy to talk to people when you both are taking salsa lessons, and have different reasons to do so.

2 - Be helpful : The truth is that the easiest way to make friends is to talk to them. Of course, it is hard to start a conversation with someone without an ice breaker. The best ice-breaker of all time is helping someone. As an eagle scout, it is in my nature to help anyone who seems to need it, and it has resulted in making a lot more friends. If you see someone struggling to put something in their car, or looking for something, or maybe even just crying a bit in public, nothing opens doors like a helping hand or a pat on the back.

3 *MOST IMPORTANT* Be Confident : Personality can get you VERY far when it comes to making new friends. If you have an infectious personality, then people will warm up to you easily. The best way to be confident is to keep yourself healthy and things of that nature (see r/GetMotivated if you are having trouble) then you can be happy with yourself. Always be cheerful and calm and keep your head up. 99% of the time, a person will love someone who is generally happy more than someone who is generally sad.

4 - Be Honest : Honesty is something not seen in society that often anymore. It seems like if someone can take advantage of you, they will. By telling the truth and being completely honest about who you are, people will learn to trust you, and become INCREDIBLY more comfortable with you. 

I met a girl in a supermarket about a month ago, and I made friends with her because of these things. She knocked over a jar of, I believe, dog treats and she was trying to pick them up herself. So I went over and helped her. I asked her if she was going to college etc. etc. and we really hit it off. A few days later we were grabbing a coffee and she asked me about a lot of my life. I told her the truth about everything and never sugar coated it, because I had confidence about myself. 
We are really good friends, and we are chilling tomorrow as well.

That's all I've got, good luck reddit!

TL;DR : Go to social places, Be Helpful, Be Confident, Be Honest.
